idea.description: Add history-conditioned gates over causal dilation scales inside one NextItNet residual block. All branches belong to one jointly trained network, yielding one feature representation and one item score. Compare adaptive gates with uniform and history-independent gates to distinguish conditioning from additional capacity.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale-interest persistence and broad relevance displacing specific recent matches. Adaptive transformations of sequential context could address both, but this mechanism requires measurement: shallow dilation over deep representations does not isolate recent interactions. Electronics’ negative tenth-percentile margin motivates improving discrimination of confusing pairs. Neither the supplied diagnostics nor related papers establish an HR@10 benefit. Mean pairwise cosine near zero also does not rule out dimensional collapse, so geometry remains an open diagnostic question.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture: start from the host’s corrected NextItNet baseline. Replace only its final residual block initially, preserving all preceding blocks, embedding dimension, residual conventions, dropout and training loss. Each parallel branch receives the same block input h and contains two channel-normalized, activated causal convolutions with kernel 3 and dilations (d, 2d), for d in {1,2,4}. Use stride 1, explicit left padding (k−1)d for each convolution and no right padding. LayerNorm operates across channels at each position only. Mask padding after normalization/activation and after each convolution, before another temporal operation; mask the residual output as well. Keep item embedding row zero fixed at zero. With inherited receptive-field span R_in, branch spans are R_in+6d, and the parallel block has maximum span R_in+24; parallel spans are not summed. Accessible offsets may contain gaps.

Gate: compute a masked causal mean c_t over h[max(0,t−3):t+1], dividing by the number of valid entries, clamped to at least one. Compute three gate logits using Linear(2D,D), GELU and Linear(D,3) on concat(h_t,c_t), followed by softmax. Initialize the final gate projection and bias to zero, producing uniform initial weights; earlier gate parameters receive gradients after that projection begins updating. This four-position summary is causal and does not extend beyond the maximum branch span, but both h_t and c_t inherit earlier dependencies. Do not describe gate weights as direct measurements of recency, purpose or intent. Sum the weighted branch outputs, add the baseline residual and mask. Use the baseline remaining output transformations and score head.

Controls and budget: retain the original model and compare identical branches with fixed uniform gates, learned global gate logits, and history-conditioned gates. A useful parameter-matched wider baseline is a secondary capacity control, rather than mandatory if it would displace the primary contrasts. Each variant is trained independently for comparison and is never fused with another model. Before execution, fix the configuration list, maximum trial count, checkpoint rule and GPU-second allocation within the shared 43,200-second budget; include diagnostics and failed trials. Keep optimizer, negative sampling, epochs and selection schedule identical across primary contrasts. Freeze numerical optimizer and dropout settings to the supplied baseline rather than inventing unspecified values. Do not introduce multiple-negative loss or text features in the first contrast. Log all attempts, parameter counts, training time and actual epochs; disclose incomplete or unequal runs. Preserve the host checkpoint-selection rule, using the same validation schedule and deterministic tie rule for every variant.

Protocol and deployment: retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; at most 200 epochs; 200 batches per epoch; single-GPU execution; DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch and ModelView. Position t predicts the next item; never expose that target through the input or a noncausal gate. Read the maximum index with a nonzero item ID, never count−1; retain the baseline’s explicit empty-history fallback. Store architecture version, selected block, dilation pairs, normalization and gate configuration with each checkpoint. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical definitions, and verify evaluation-mode feature and candidate-score parity after save/reload. The deployed predictor loads exactly one selected independently trained checkpoint per category. Do not use independent scoring components, checkpoint averaging, or other trials’ checkpoints.

Diagnostics: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors; view.model remains the actual trained module. Return measured metrics and definitions. Preserve sampled margin diagnostics and their sampling procedure; do not equate them with pinned candidate ranking. Categories, reviews, ratings, prices and stores are unavailable: mark their breakdowns unavailable, and never manufacture them. Titles/descriptions and public training histories/timestamps are the only permitted auxiliary data.

Geometry and scale: separately sample nonpadding item embeddings and final history features with fixed diagnostic randomness. Report centered singular values, total variance, leading-component variance share, norm quantiles and cosine distributions. Define covariance effective rank as exp(−sum p_i log p_i), where p_i=s_i²/sum s_j²; mark it undefined if variance is zero. This differs from RankMe’s singular-value normalization. Low rank alone does not establish harmful collapse. Where the host exposes permitted fixed validation candidate scores, report candidate-logit standard deviation, positive-minus-largest-negative and positive-minus-tenth-largest-negative margins, plus angular separation for the same pairs. These distinguish geometry from score scale. Temperature-only rescaling preserves rank and cannot improve HR@10 by itself.

Mechanism and uncertainty: freeze checkpoints and use identical permitted validation users, targets and candidates for recent-k-only, equally sized old/recent block removal, and within-block shuffling. Preserve the final item when testing earlier order, use length-matched replacement controls, and state each intervention’s changed inputs. The baseline receptive field bounds detectable older-history effects. Shuffling gate assignments across histories is supplementary because it induces distribution shift. These interventions measure model dependence, not causal effects on users, and must not alter the official evaluator or main selection inputs. If the host does not expose these diagnostic hooks, report them unavailable rather than rebuilding or changing the evaluator. Additional evaluations consume the same budget.

When paired host validation hit indicators are available, compute the mean of four within-category mean hit differences, report category deltas and discordant wins/losses, and bootstrap paired users within category using 2,000 resamples and diagnostic seed 42 for percentile 95% intervals. These intervals condition on trained checkpoints and fixed candidates; they omit training randomness, candidate variability and adaptive-selection bias. They characterize pinned sampled HR@10, not full-catalog accuracy. Prespecify contrasts and stopping, disclose validation reuse, and reserve confirmation for the untouched host final evaluation.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify variants, checkpoint rule and shared GPU-second allocations.
For each permitted variant and category:
    initialize one corrected NextItNet model with training seed 42
    for each permitted training batch:
        mask = sequence.ne(0)[..., None]
        h = baseline_embedding_and_preceding_blocks(sequence, mask)
        context = masked_causal_mean(h, mask, window=4)
        if variant == uniform:
            weights = [1/3, 1/3, 1/3]
        elif variant == static:
            weights = softmax(learned_global_logits)
        elif variant == adaptive:
            weights = softmax(gate(concat(h, context)), dim=-1)
        branches = []
        for d in [1, 2, 4]:
            z = h
            for dilation in [d, 2*d]:
                z = channel_layernorm_then_activation(z) * mask
                z = conv1d(left_pad(z, 2*dilation), kernel=3,
                           dilation=dilation, right_padding=0) * mask
            branches.append(z)
        mixed = sum(weights[..., k:k+1] * branches[k] for k in range(3))
        h = (h + baseline_residual_dropout(mixed)) * mask
        features = baseline_output_transform(h) * mask
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
        update all network parameters jointly
    apply the unchanged host validation and checkpoint-selection protocol
    save one selected state and complete architecture configuration
    reconstruct through the embedded predictor; verify feature/score parity
Compare variants using host macro validation HR@10; record every attempt.
Run budgeted, supported diagnostics without changing official evaluation.
Deploy one selected checkpoint per category.
At prediction, read max(index where sequence != 0), with baseline empty-history handling.

originality.positive: The adaptation permits a controlled study of input-conditioned convolution scales within the required NextItNet family.
originality.negative: Selective Kernel Networks already establish input-conditioned multiscale branch weighting, so novelty is primarily the task-specific adaptation and evaluation.

future_potential.positive: Static-gate controls and history interventions could clarify when adaptive context transformations help sequential recommendation.
future_potential.negative: Gates may become effectively static; overlapping inherited context limits recency interpretation, and benefits on sampled validation may not generalize.

code_difficulty.positive: The architecture change is localized, retains the baseline objective and uses standard convolution, normalization and softmax operations.
code_difficulty.negative: Intermediate padding masks, causal dependencies, architecture serialization, predictor parity and budgeted controls make the full experiment moderately demanding.

report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **history-conditioned dilation gates inside NextItNet**, with multiple-negative softmax as the next alternative. No validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Users identify stale interests and broad relevance displacing specific recent matches; context dependence warrants testing. (2) Electronics has 12.27% sampled ranking errors and a −0.2595 tenth-percentile margin; these measure sampled training separation, not validation performance. (3) Cosine-derived scores of 0.5071–0.5234 indicate little mean directional alignment, but cannot exclude dimensional collapse.

**Insights from related work.** (1) NextItNet supplies causal residual convolutions [1]. (2) Selective Kernel Networks directly precede input-conditioned scale weighting; FADC supplies cross-domain motivation [2,4], reducing originality claims. (3) Sampled-softmax research supports multiple negatives, with temperature sensitivity [3]. None establishes gains here.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing ingredient | Proposed experiment | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context selection | NextItNet; selective kernels; FADC | Position-dependent dilation gates | Inherited context prevents literal recency interpretation |
| Ranking objective | Sampled softmax | Uniform multiple-negative training | False negatives and temperature |
| Item identity | Text-enhanced recommendation | Jointly trained title encoder | Sparse supervision; compatibility unobserved |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension includes a positive and negative consideration.

1. **Dilation gates: 4/6/7/6/5.** Originality: task-specific adaptation / established selective kernels. Potential: testable context adaptation / gates may become static. User alignment: targets stale interests and purpose mismatch / cannot verify compatibility. Model alignment: may resolve ambiguity / margins need not generalize. Difficulty: localized change / causality and predictor parity need care.
2. **Multiple-negative softmax: 3/7/5/9/3.** Originality: useful adaptation / established objective. Potential: efficient competition / sampling sensitivity. User alignment: ranks alternatives / weak intent specificity. Model alignment: targets separation / sampled margins can mislead. Difficulty: small loss change / exclusion bookkeeping.
3. **Trainable title encoder: 4/6/8/6/6.** Originality: constrained adaptation / familiar fusion. Potential: item identity / limited supervision. User alignment: purpose cues / compatibility unknown. Model alignment: distinguishes items / metadata noise. Difficulty: lightweight encoder / vocabulary and predictor changes.

**Selected experiment.** Replace one residual block with jointly trained causal dilation branches and position-dependent gates. This explicitly targets stale-interest persistence and broad relevance displacing immediate-purpose matches; Electronics’ weak lower-tail separation supplies the model-facing target. These are hypotheses: small dilations over deep features still inherit older context.

Initialize gates uniformly; retain the loss. Prespecify baseline, uniform, static-learned and history-conditioned comparisons, plus a parameter-matched capacity control if budget permits. Match training and selection budgets; report parameters and compute. Use recent/old-block ablations to test history dependence and singular spectra to assess geometry. Gate weights alone cannot establish intent.

Keep one network/checkpoint per category, all protocol limits and final-nonpadding readout. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Report paired category deltas and stratified-bootstrap intervals conditional on checkpoints/candidates; selection bias remains. Log every attempt and reserve confirmation for untouched host evaluation.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369; [3] https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf; [4] https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.06586.
